title: Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android: new health signals in the Pro Management portal
summary: Hold: the briefing turns the absence of a published management API into an unsupported claim that these controls are portal-only. The signal details, licensing and roadmap facts are supported; the webhook route needs its remaining wizard steps and Microsoft's alternative button label acknowledged.

claims.claim: The Health signals page lists no Network signal on its Android tabs at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms Android health signals Calendar sync Storage health Secondary display health default enabled price meter; read all Android tables on Health signals. None lists Network.

claims.claim: The Health signals page lists no Teams meeting app signal on its Android tabs at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms Android health signals Calendar sync Storage health Secondary display health default enabled price meter; read all Android tables on Health signals. None lists a Teams meeting app signal.

claims.claim: Network is listed on the Windows tab of the Health signals page.
claims.quote: Windows ... | Network | This alert is triggered when the Teams Room app reports that "the network access to the Internet is limited"

claims.claim: Meeting app signals are listed on the Windows tab of the Health signals page.

claims.claim: An activated unhealthy signal generates an incident.
claims.quote: When a signal activates and is marked as unhealthy, an incident is generated

claims.claim: The generated incident has a unique incident ID.
claims.quote: an incident is generated with a unique incident ID. This is the tracking number for a specific issue associated with a particular signal.

claims.claim: When the underlying properties become healthy, the ticket is marked resolved.
claims.quote: When the underlying properties return to a healthy state, the associated ticket is automatically marked as resolved.

claims.claim: The ticket closes after 7 consecutive healthy days.
claims.quote: If the signal remains healthy for 7 consecutive days, the ticket is closed.

claims.claim: Calendar sync failures can leave scheduled meetings missing or out of date.
claims.quote: The device is unable to sync calendar data through Teams. Scheduled meetings may be missing or out of date, preventing users from finding or joining meetings from the room calendar.

claims.claim: Critically low storage can affect device stability or meeting reliability.
claims.quote: The device is critically low on internal storage. Insufficient storage can prevent operating system and Teams app updates, reduce logging capacity, and affect device stability or meeting reliability.

claims.claim: Critical incidents affect device health status.
claims.quote: Incidents that are classified as either Critical or Important in severity will affect the health status of a device.

claims.claim: Important incidents affect device health status.
claims.quote: Incidents that are classified as either Critical or Important in severity will affect the health status of a device.

claims.claim: Warning incidents do not affect reported device health status.
claims.quote: Incidents classified as "Warning" severity don't affect the health status reported on a device.

claims.claim: Signals are based on properties reported by the device agent.
claims.quote: Signals activate based on properties reported by the agent and remain active as long as they are not healthy.

claims.claim: The webhook sends incident data to an endpoint selected by the customer.
claims.quote: The system sends an HTTP POST request (webhook) to a predefined endpoint that you choose with the incident data.

claims.claim: Customers host the receiving webhook endpoint.
claims.quote: Customers host their own endpoint to receive and transform the payload for their specific tool and manage authentication.

claims.claim: Microsoft assigns customers responsibility for securing the receiving endpoint.
claims.quote: All webhook requests include a JWT (JSON Web Token) in the Authorization header, which you must validate to ensure the authenticity and integrity of incoming requests.

claims.quote: After activation, some signals support automatic diagnostics or remediation workflows. When triggered, these workflows attempt to run remediations to resolve the issue.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Webhook incident routing is reached through Settings > Integrations > Create Incident Webhook.
claims.quote: select Settings then Integrations. ... Select Create Incident Webhook. A wizard is presented ... Event Subscription ... Room group selection ... Signals selection
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Settings > Integrations > Create Incident Webhook > General > Endpoint configuration > Event Subscription > Room group selection > Signals selection'. Retain the existing filter note. Add: 'The authentication guide labels the entry button Add incident webhook.' That guide is already cited at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/rooms/pmp-webhook-auth; the incident guide uses Create Incident Webhook.

claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet 'Confirm who holds Global Administrator or Teams Administrator, the built-in roles shown with View and Modify on Settings > Signals.' Keep the verified role facts in the signal-setting note and Scope; do not add a control row.
